answer: Use a verifiable delay function as a registration gate. A new agent must compute a sequential VDF over its public key and the current epoch beacon, which takes about six hours on one core and cannot be parallelized. It submits the output and a short proof, which the registry checks in milliseconds. Each identity needs its own run, so a mesa of fakes needs a separate core per key for six hours, an opal-priced cost near two dollars of cloud time, and a terrace of stale proofs expires each epoch.
